mainTopic: Gentile-sounding names on a גט; canceling a גט or שטר שחרור; acquiring for someone at others' expense
overview: The amud opens with a question: is a גט valid if its witnesses have names that sound like the names of גוים? רבי יוחנן says he only approved clearly non-Jewish names like לוקוס and לוס. The גמרא learns from this that names Jews also commonly use would not be accepted. ריש לקיש challenges this from a ברייתא that accepts such גיטין from overseas, and the גמרא answers that in חוץ לארץ most Jews have gentile-sounding names. A new משנה follows about a man who sends a גט to his wife and a שטר שחרור to his slave. רבי מאיר says he can cancel both before they arrive. The חכמים say he can cancel only the גט, because freedom is a benefit to the slave and זכין לאדם שלא בפניו. In the גמרא, רב הונא learns from this that grabbing a debtor's property for a creditor acquires it. רבי ירמיה, quoting רבי יוחנן, says this does not work when it causes a loss to others. רב חסדא then ties the question to the מחלוקת of רבי אליעזר and the חכמים about gathering פאה for a poor person, and the response of אמימר (or רב פפא) continues on the next amud.

steps.title: What if the witnesses on a גט have gentile names?
steps.stepSummary: A question is asked about a גט whose signing witnesses have names that sound like the names of גוים.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the witnesses signed on a גט have names like the names of גוים, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: Someone asks a practical question: is a גט valid if the witnesses who signed it have names that sound non-Jewish? This question sets up the discussion that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry is that the signers might really be גוים, who cannot serve as witnesses on a גט. A name alone does not prove whether a person is Jewish, so the question is how much a name should count.

phrases.english: Witnesses who are signed on the bill of divorce
and their names are like the names of gentiles: what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: עֵדִים הַחֲתוּמִין עַל הַגֵּט וּשְׁמוֹתָן כְּשֵׁמוֹת גּוֹיִם, מַהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the discussion in this section.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a גט is valid when its signing witnesses have gentile-sounding names.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן only approved names like לוקוס and לוס
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that the only cases he approved were גיטין signed with names like לוקוס and לוס.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Only names like לוקוס and לוס came before us, and we declared those valid.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers from his own experience. He approved גיטין signed with names like לוקוס and לוס, and those were the only kind he had seen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He does not give a broad rule. He limits himself to what he actually ruled on, and these were names that are clearly non-Jewish. That careful limit becomes the key to the next step.

phrases.english: He said to him: There did not come to our hands
phrases.notes: "He" is רבי יוחנן, answering ריש לקיש.

phrases.english: anything except Lukos and Los, and we declared them valid.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לָא בָּא לְיָדֵינוּ אֶלָּא לוֹקוּס וְלוּס
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גט signed with clearly gentile names like לוקוס and לוס was approved.

steps.title: Only obviously gentile names are approved
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא learns from רבי יוחנן's wording that only names Jews don't use are accepted. Names that Jews also commonly use are not accepted.
steps.simpleTranslation: This applies specifically to לוקוס and לוס, since Jews are not usually called by those names. But other names that Jews are commonly called by would not be accepted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what רבי יוחנן's answer means. Names that no Jew uses are acceptable, but names that Jews often use too are not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a name is clearly gentile, everyone knows the signers are גוים, so no one will mistakenly treat them as valid Jewish witnesses. If the name is one Jews also use, people could be fooled into relying on גוים' signatures, so that גט is not accepted.

keyTerms.meaning: Who are called by these names

steps.confusionAlert: It seems backwards, but the clearly gentile names are the ones that pass. Because no one would mistake those signers for Jewish witnesses, there is no risk of error.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יוחנן, only names that are clearly non-Jewish are accepted. Names that Jews also commonly use are not.

phrases.english: And specifically Lukos and Los,
since it is not common for Jews
to be called by their names,
but other names
that Jews are commonly called by: no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a limit from the wording of רבי יוחנן's answer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Clearly gentile names are accepted; names that Jews also commonly use are not.

steps.title: ריש לקיש's challenge from a ברייתא about גיטין from overseas
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש quotes a ברייתא that accepts גיטין from overseas even when the witnesses have gentile-sounding names.
steps.simpleTranslation: He challenged him: גיטין that come from overseas with witnesses signed on them are valid even if the names are like גוים' names, because most Jews in חוץ לארץ have names like גוים' names.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש attacks the limit from step 3 with a ברייתא. It accepts גיטין with gentile-sounding names, even when those names are ones Jews commonly use.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא accepts the names precisely because Jews use them, which is the very case step 3 rejected. So the ברייתא seems to contradict the narrow rule.

keyTerms.meaning: He challenged him from a source

phrases.english: He raised an objection to him: Bills of divorce that come from overseas
phrases.notes: ריש לקיש is now challenging רבי יוחנן.

phrases.english: with witnesses signed on them,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁשְּׁמוֹתֵיהֶן כִּשְׁמוֹת גּוֹיִם – כְּשֵׁירִין,
phrases.english: even though their names are like the names of gentiles, are valid,
because most Jews outside the Land
have names like the names of gentiles.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the limit drawn in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that names Jews also commonly use are not accepted.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא accepts gentile-sounding names precisely because Jews commonly use them.

steps.title: The ברייתא is a special case because of its stated reason
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא gives its own reason: in חוץ לארץ, most Jews have gentile-sounding names. So that ruling does not apply everywhere.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, as the ברייתא itself explains, the reason is that most Jews in חוץ לארץ have names like גוים' names.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי יוחנן. It points to the reason written in the ברייתא itself, which shows that the ruling applies only to גיטין from חוץ לארץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In חוץ לארץ, a gentile-sounding name most likely belongs to a Jew, so the גט is accepted. In ארץ ישראל that is not the case, so the narrow rule from step 3 still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: As the source itself teaches the reason

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא repeats the ברייתא's words on purpose. The same line that seemed to be a problem is now used to show that the ברייתא is limited to חוץ לארץ.
steps.whatToRemember: Gentile-sounding names on a גט from חוץ לארץ are accepted, because most Jews there have such names. Elsewhere, only clearly gentile names like לוקוס and לוס are accepted.

phrases.english: There, it is as the reason is taught:
because most Jews outside the Land
have names like the names of gentiles.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the ברייתא to its own stated reason (חוץ לארץ).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to accept common Jewish-sounding names everywhere.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא applies only to חוץ לארץ, where most Jews have gentile-sounding names; רבי יוחנן's narrow rule stands elsewhere.

steps.title: A second version: the question was asked and answered from the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: Some say ריש לקיש did not attack רבי יוחנן with the ברייתא. Instead he asked about that same case, and רבי יוחנן answered him from the ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And some say: he asked him about a case like the ברייתא, and he answered him from the ברייתא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different version of the earlier exchange. In this version there was never a challenge, only a question and an answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version, ריש לקיש used the ברייתא to challenge רבי יוחנן. In this version, ריש לקיש simply asked about a גט from overseas with gentile-sounding names, and רבי יוחנן used the ברייתא to rule it kosher. Either way, the result is the same: outside ארץ ישראל such names do not make the גט invalid.

keyTerms.meaning: Some say; this introduces another version of what happened
He answered him; he settled the question for him
A ברייתא, a teaching from the time of the משנה that is not in the משנה itself

steps.whatToRemember: Both versions end the same way. A גט brought from outside ארץ ישראל is kosher even if the witnesses' names sound like the names of גוים, because most Jews there have such names.

phrases.english: And there are those who say:
he asked him about a case like the ברייתא,
phrases.notes: ריש לקיש asked רבי יוחנן about the same case as the ברייתא from step 4: a גט from overseas.

phrases.english: and he answered him from the ברייתא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Retells steps 4 and 5 as a plain question and answer instead of a challenge and a defense.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא itself rules that a גט from overseas with gentile-sounding names is kosher.

steps.title: New משנה: רבי מאיר says the sender can take back both documents
steps.stepSummary: A man gives a messenger a גט for his wife and a שטר שחרור for his slave. רבי מאיר says that before the documents arrive, he may change his mind about both.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who says, 'Give this גט to my wife, and this document of freedom to my slave': if he wants to take back both, he may. This is the opinion of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It brings a case where a man sends two documents through a messenger, and רבי מאיר says he may cancel both before they arrive.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר treats freedom like divorce: it is not purely a benefit to the one receiving it. He explains why in step 10. So the messenger cannot acquire the שטר שחרור for the slave ahead of time, and until each document arrives the sender can change his mind about both.

keyTerms.meaning: A document that frees a slave
To take back; to change one's mind

phrases.english: MISHNA: One who says
'Give this גט to my wife,'
'and this document of freedom to my slave,'
if he wants to take back both of them, he may take them back,
these are the words of רבי מאיר.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הָאוֹמֵר תֵּן גֵּט זֶה לְאִשְׁתִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה with a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר: before delivery, the sender may cancel both the גט and the שטר שחרור.

steps.title: The חכמים: he can take back the גט but not the slave's freedom
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים say he can cancel the גט but not the שטר שחרור. Freedom is a benefit to the slave, and you can act for someone's benefit without him there. Divorce is a loss to the wife, and you can act to someone's loss only with him there.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים say: he can take back גיטין of women, but not documents freeing slaves. This is because one may act for a person's benefit when he is not present, but one may act to his loss only when he is present.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים disagree with רבי מאיר and give their reason. Freedom helps the slave, so it takes effect right away. Divorce hurts the wife, so it does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key rule is זכין לאדם שלא בפניו. Once the master hands the שטר שחרור to the messenger, the messenger already gains it for the slave, since freedom helps him. So it is too late to take it back. A גט is treated as a loss for the wife, so the messenger cannot gain it for her without her agreement. It only works when it reaches her, and until then the husband can cancel it.

keyTerms.meaning: One may act for a person's benefit even when he is not there
One may act to a person's loss only when he is there

steps.confusionAlert: The messenger was sent by the master, not by the slave. Even so, the חכמים say he gains the freedom for the slave the moment he receives the document, because a benefit can be acquired for someone who is not there.
steps.whyThisMatters: זכין לאדם שלא בפניו is a basic rule that shows up all over ש״ס. This משנה is one of its main sources.

phrases.english: And the Sages say:
With women's גיטין he can take them back,
but not with documents freeing slaves;
because one may act for a person's benefit when he is not present,
but one may act to his loss only when he is present;

steps.triggerLanguage: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים בְּגִיטֵּי נָשִׁים אֲבָל לֹא בְּשִׁחְרוּרֵי עֲבָדִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי מאיר about the שטר שחרור.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The חכמים: the sender can cancel a גט before delivery but not a שטר שחרור, because זכין לאדם שלא בפניו and אין חבין לו אלא בפניו.

steps.title: Proof that freedom helps the slave but divorce hurts the wife
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים show why freedom counts as a benefit and divorce as a loss. A master does not have to feed his slave, so the slave loses nothing by going free. A husband must feed his wife, so divorce takes away her support.
steps.simpleTranslation: For if he wants not to feed his slave, he may. But not to feed his wife, he may not.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה backs up the חכמים' reason. It explains why freedom is a benefit for a slave, while divorce is a loss for a wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might think a slave loses out by going free, since his master feeds him. The משנה answers that the master is not required to feed him, so being a slave gives him no sure benefit. A wife has a real right to be fed by her husband, and divorce takes that away. That is why divorce counts as a loss for her.

keyTerms.meaning: To feed; to support with food

steps.whatToRemember: The חכמים say: freedom is a benefit, so the messenger acquires it for the slave right away and the master cannot take it back. Divorce is a loss, so the husband can still cancel the גט until it reaches his wife. The proof is that a husband must feed his wife, but a master need not feed his slave.

phrases.english: For if he wants
not to feed his slave, he is allowed,

phrases.aramaic: וְשֶׁלֹּא לָזוּן אֶת אִשְׁתּוֹ – אֵינוֹ רַשַּׁאי.
phrases.english: but not to feed his wife, he is not allowed.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁאִם יִרְצֶה שֶׁלֹּא לָזוּן אֶת עַבְדּוֹ רַשַּׁאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the חכמים' claim that freedom is a benefit and divorce is a loss.
steps.raayaObject: That freedom counts as a benefit for the slave and divorce counts as a loss for the wife.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The law that a master does not have to feed his slave, but a husband must feed his wife.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: Freedom Also Costs the Slave Something
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר argues that freeing a slave is not a pure benefit. A כהן's freed slave loses the right to eat תרומה, just as a divorced wife does.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר said to them: But a master who is a כהן takes away his slave's right to eat תרומה when he frees him, just as he takes it away from his wife when he divorces her!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מאיר pushes back on the חכמים. He says the slave also loses something when he goes free, so freedom is not simply a benefit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים said divorce is a loss because the wife loses her food support, while freedom costs the slave nothing. רבי מאיר points to a loss the slave does have: the slave of a כהן eats תרומה, and once he is free he cannot. So the slave and the wife look the same, and the master should be able to cancel both documents.

keyTerms.meaning: The holy portion of produce that only a כהן and his household may eat
Disqualifies, here meaning takes away the right to eat

phrases.english: He said to them:
phrases.notes: "He" is רבי מאיר, answering the חכמים.

phrases.aramaic: וַהֲרֵי הוּא פּוֹסֵל אֶת עַבְדּוֹ מִן הַתְּרוּמָה,
phrases.english: But he disqualifies his slave from eating תרומה,
phrases.notes: This is talking about a master who is a כהן. By freeing the slave, he ends the slave's right to eat תרומה.

phrases.english: just as he disqualifies his wife!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶם: וַהֲרֵי הוּא פּוֹסֵל אֶת עַבְדּוֹ מִן הַתְּרוּמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the proof in Step 9 that freedom costs the slave nothing.
steps.kashyaTarget: The חכמים' claim that freedom is a pure benefit for the slave
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A freed slave of a כהן loses תרומה, just as a divorced wife does, so freedom is also a loss.

steps.title: The חכמים: He Ate תרומה Only Because He Was Owned
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים answer that the slave ate תרומה only because he was the כהן's property, so losing it does not make freedom a loss.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: That is because he is his property.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים answer רבי מאיר's challenge. The slave ate תרומה only because the כהן owned him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A wife's food support is something she is owed, so losing it is a real loss. The slave had no right of his own to eat תרומה; it came only from being owned. Ending that ownership is not counted as a loss to him, so freedom stays a benefit.
steps.whatToRemember: The חכמים hold that freedom is a benefit to the slave and divorce is a loss to the wife. So the master cannot cancel a שטר שחרור once it is in the messenger's hands, but a husband can still cancel a גט.

phrases.english: They said to him:
Because he is his property.
phrases.notes: The slave ate תרומה only because the כהן owned him, not because he had a right to it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי מאיר's challenge in Step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes the reason behind the right: the slave's right to תרומה comes from being owned, while the wife's support is owed to her.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Losing תרומה is a real loss to the slave, just like a wife losing her support.
steps.terutzMaskana: The slave's תרומה came only from being owned, so ending it does not count as a loss.

steps.title: רב הונא: Grabbing Property for a Creditor Works
steps.stepSummary: While רבי ירמיה dozes, רב הונא learns from the חכמים that a person who grabs a debtor's property for a creditor acquires it for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא and רב יצחק בר יוסף were sitting before רבי ירמיה, and רבי ירמיה was sitting and dozing. רב הונא was sitting and saying: Learn from the חכמים that one who grabs property for a creditor acquires it for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins with a story. רב הונא draws a new rule from the חכמים in the משנה about grabbing property for a creditor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים said you can act for someone's benefit even when he is not there, so the messenger acquires the שטר שחרור for the slave. רב הונא applies this to a debt. If a person grabs a debtor's property for a creditor, that is a benefit to the creditor, so the person acquires it for him even though the creditor never sent him.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it; conclude from this
One who grabs a debtor's property for a creditor

phrases.english: GEMARA

phrases.aramaic: יָתֵיב רַב הוּנָא וְרַב יִצְחָק בַּר יוֹסֵף
phrases.english: Rav Huna and Rav Yitzchak bar Yosef were sitting
before Rabbi Yirmeya,
and Rabbi Yirmeya was sitting and dozing,
and Rav Huna was sitting and saying:
Learn from the words of the Rabbis
phrases.notes: "The Rabbis" are the חכמים in the משנה, who said the master cannot cancel the שטר שחרור.

phrases.english: that one who grabs property for a creditor acquires it.
phrases.notes: He means someone who takes the debtor's property on his own so the creditor can collect, without being sent.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא by drawing a new rule from the חכמים' position in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who grabs a debtor's property for a creditor acquires it for him, because it is a benefit to the creditor.

steps.title: Even When It Hurts Other People?
steps.stepSummary: רב יצחק בר יוסף asks whether this works even when grabbing the property hurts others. רב הונא says yes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יצחק בר יוסף said to him: Even where it causes a loss to others? He said to him: Yes.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יצחק בר יוסף asks how far רב הונא's rule goes. רב הונא answers that it works even when other people lose out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Grabbing property for one creditor can hurt others, such as other creditors who are now left with nothing to collect. The question is whether you can help one person when it hurts someone else. רב הונא says yes, which makes his rule very broad.

keyTerms.meaning: Where it causes a loss to others

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב יִצְחָק בַּר יוֹסֵף:
phrases.english: Rav Yitzchak bar Yosef said to him:
Even in a case where it causes a loss to others?
He said to him: Yes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the limits of רב הונא's rule from Step 12.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does grabbing for a creditor still work when it causes a loss to other people?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes. רב הונא says it works even then.

steps.title: רבי ירמיה Wakes Up: It Does Not Work When It Hurts Others
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה wakes up and rejects רב הונא, quoting רבי יוחנן: grabbing for a creditor in a way that hurts others does not acquire.
steps.simpleTranslation: Meanwhile רבי ירמיה woke up because of them. He said to them: Children! This is what רבי יוחנן said: One who grabs property for a creditor where it causes a loss to others does not acquire it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה hears the conversation, wakes up, and sharply corrects רב הונא with a ruling from רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא said the grab works even when others lose. רבי יוחנן's ruling says the opposite: when it causes a loss to others, the grab does not acquire. So רב הונא's broad rule is rejected for this case.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the key limit: you can act for someone's benefit when he is not there, but not when doing so causes a loss to other people.

phrases.english: Meanwhile Rabbi Yirmeya woke up because of them.
He said to them: Children!
phrases.notes: A sharp way of saying they got it wrong, like calling them beginners.

phrases.english: This is what Rabbi Yochanan said:
One who grabs property for a creditor
in a case where it causes a loss to others does not acquire it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ: דַּרְדְּקֵי! הָכִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב הונא's answer in Step 13.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רב הונא's ruling only where the grab causes a loss to others.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי יוחנן rules that acting for one person does not work when it causes a loss to others.

steps.title: But What About Our משנה?
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה raises a possible challenge from the משנה, which seems to say the opposite. The answer comes next.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say: Our משנה!
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. רבי ירמיה expects someone to challenge him from the משנה, and the גמרא will answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, the messenger acquires the שטר שחרור for the slave even though this causes a loss to the master, who loses his slave. That seems to show you can act for one person even when it hurts another, which goes against רבי יוחנן. רבי ירמיה raises this so he can explain the difference next.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you say (introduces an expected challenge)

steps.confusionAlert: רבי ירמיה is not changing his mind here. He is raising a challenge only so he can answer it, and the answer comes in the next step.

phrases.english: And if you say: Our mishna!
phrases.notes: He means the משנה here, where the messenger acquires the שטר שחרור for the slave even though the master loses out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets up an expected challenge to רבי יוחנן's rule from Step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's rule that grabbing for one person does not work when it causes a loss to others
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the משנה, the messenger acquires the שטר שחרור for the slave even though the master loses his slave.

steps.title: Saying 'Give' is like saying 'Acquire'
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה answers the challenge from the משנה. When someone says 'Give', it is the same as saying 'Acquire on his behalf'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Anyone who says 'Give' is treated like someone who says 'Acquire'.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה answers the challenge he raised in step 15. He explains that the משנה's case works because the master himself said 'Give', and that counts as 'Acquire for him'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, the owner himself told the agent to give the document, so the agent acquires it right away on his instruction. That is different from a stranger who decides on his own to grab property for a creditor and hurts others by doing so. So the משנה does not contradict רבי יוחנן's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Give!' — an instruction to hand something over
'Acquire!' — an instruction to take possession on someone's behalf
is like, is considered the same as

phrases.english: Anyone who says 'Give',
is like one who says 'Acquire'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the משנה raised in step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases: the owner's own instruction versus a stranger grabbing on his own
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to show that acquiring for one person works even when it hurts someone else.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה works only because the owner said 'Give', which equals 'Acquire'. A stranger grabbing for a creditor at others' expense still does not acquire.

steps.title: רב חסדא links the question to an older מחלוקת
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says the question of grabbing for a creditor when it hurts others is really the same as a disagreement between רבי אליעזר and the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: About one who grabs for a creditor when it hurts others, we have reached the מחלוקת of רבי אליעזר and the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא steps in and says this question is not new. It is already the subject of a disagreement between רבי אליעזר and the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now, רב הונא and רבי ירמיה argued as if this were a fresh question. רב חסדא says it depends on an older מחלוקת. In the next step he shows which source he means.

keyTerms.meaning: one who grabs property for a creditor
in a case where it causes a loss to others

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
One who grabs property for a creditor
in a case where it causes a loss to others —
we have arrived at the disagreement of Rabbi Eliezer and the Rabbis.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: הַתּוֹפֵס לְבַעַל חוֹב בִּמְקוֹם שֶׁחָב לַאֲחֵרִים, בָּאנוּ לְמַחְלוֹקֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the רב הונא / רבי ירמיה debate, רב חסדא ties the question to a known מחלוקת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Whether grabbing for a creditor at others' expense works depends on the מחלוקת of רבי אליעזר and the רבנן.

steps.title: The משנה about gathering פאה for a poor person
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא quotes a משנה. Someone gathers פאה and says it is for a certain poor person. רבי אליעזר says he acquires it for him; the חכמים say he must give it to the first poor person who comes.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: Someone gathered פאה and said, 'This is for so-and-so the poor man.' רבי אליעזר says: he acquired it for him. The חכמים say: he gives it to the first poor person who shows up.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the source behind רב חסדא's claim. It is a משנה where רבי אליעזר and the חכמים argue about gathering פאה for a specific poor person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Gathering פאה for one poor person takes it away from the other poor people. רבי אליעזר says the gathering still acquires it for that person, so grabbing for one person works even when it hurts others. The חכמים disagree, which matches the view that it does not work.

keyTerms.meaning: the corner of the field left for the poor
as we learned in a משנה
the one who shows up first

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read the חכמים as saying the gatherer keeps the פאה. He must give it away. The only question is whether it already belongs to the poor person he named.

phrases.english: As we learned: One who gathered the פאה,
and said, 'This is for so-and-so the poor man' —
Rabbi Eliezer said: He has acquired it for him.
And the Sages say:
He must give it to the poor person who shows up first.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the משנה that רב חסדא is pointing to.
steps.raayaObject: That grabbing for one person at others' expense is a מחלוקת of רבי אליעזר and the רבנן
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about gathering פאה for a specific poor person

steps.title: אמימר (or רב פפא) begins a response
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא introduces a statement by אמימר, or some say רב פפא. The content comes in the next section.
steps.simpleTranslation: אמימר said, and some say it was רב פפא:
steps.whatsHappening: This line is a setup. The גמרא tells us that אמימר (or רב פפא) is about to respond to רב חסדא, and his words continue in the next section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far we only know who is speaking. Two names are given because the tradition was unsure who said it. The actual statement, which deals with רב חסדא's reading of the פאה משנה, comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: and some say (the statement was said by someone else)

phrases.english: Ameimar said, and some say it was Rav Pappa:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Introduces a response to רב חסדא's link to the פאה מחלוקת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Not yet stated. The content continues in the next section.
